text:
Medicaid payments for Outpatient PPS services in Newton jump 213.6% in 2024
J. N. Kern
In 2024, Medicaid providers in Newton billed a total of $994 for Outpatient PPS-designated services, according to the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services Medicaid Provider Spending database. This represented a 213.6% jump compared to the $317 billed by providers for comparable services in 2023.
Medicaid is a public health program overseen by the states with financial backing from both federal and state governments. The program serves low-income residents, the elderly, children, and individuals with disabilities, and is one of the core components of the nation’s health care system.
Because Medicaid is taxpayer-funded, local changes in billing highlight how public resources for health care are distributed within a community.
The Outpatient PPS category includes a range of Medicaid-billed services grouped by care type, defined by standard sets of HCPCS and CPT codes. For this review, billing codes were sorted into single service categories based on identified code patterns to enable a consistent comparison and ranking over time while avoiding duplicate counting.
While overall Medicaid spending rose across various service groups, Outpatient PPS placed 15th in Newton for Medicaid payment totals in 2024.
Statewide in New Jersey, Outpatient PPS was ranked 20th by Medicaid payment totals in 2024.
From 2019 through 2024, the total Medicaid payments associated with Outpatient PPS services in Newton increased by $994, reflecting a 0% rise over the same period. Some intervals saw heightened spending growth, showing significant annual increases in both 2023 and 2022.
Although care payments in the Outpatient PPS group occurred throughout Newton, the most significant amount was concentrated within just a handful of ZIP codes. Notably, in 2024, ZIP code 07860 accounted for the $994 total. The highest-billing ZIP code made up 100% of these Medicaid payments across Newton that year.
Within Outpatient PPS, a small set of billing codes represented the majority of payments.
For context, Outpatient PPS Medicaid payments in Newton surged 213.6% from 2023 to 2024, while all Medicaid claim categories saw a combined change of 7.6% during the same time frame in the city.
Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services data show federal and state Medicaid spending reached approximately $871.7 billion for fiscal year 2023, which was nearly 18% of national health expenses, a sharp increase from the $613.5 billion recorded in 2019, before the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic.
This represents growth of around 40% in several years, largely due to more enrollees and increased service use throughout and after the pandemic’s peak.
Recent federal legislative changes under the Trump administration have featured notable federal Medicaid funding reductions and program redesigns. The “One Big Beautiful Bill Act,” enacted in 2025, is forecast to reduce federal Medicaid spending by over $1 trillion within the next decade and implement policy shifts—like work mandates and expanded cost-sharing—that may decrease funding and coverage options for certain participants. These measures are expected to increase financial responsibility for states and moderate the pace of federal support, though Medicaid will remain vital for millions nationwide.
